Aisha and team —

We implemented emergency containment at 00:55 PDT:
- Disabled scheduled quantize-warmup jobs across Novaris' Dedicated pool.
- Applied a soft pin at the routing layer to prefer nv1-live model variant for all Novaris traffic.
- Raised pool min-capacity by 20% to ensure no further churn during evening peaks.

Initial improvement: 5xx rates dropped to baseline within ~7 minutes and tail latency 99.9th dropped to ~1.1s. We've kept mitigation in place while we build the RCA.

Next steps: I'm drafting an RCA write-up and a set of corrective actions; Michael, can you coordinate the customer exec readout tomorrow at 10:00 PDT?

Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft RCA and proposed corrective actions

Team —

I've attached a short draft RCA and proposed actions; high-level summary:
1) Root cause: concurrent maintenance job (quantize warmups) consumed shared GPU memory on a subset of workers while autoscaler triggered pool rotation, which caused KV cache allocation failures and elevated request fallbacks. Timing overlap appears to be the primary driver.
2) Why it mattered: Novaris' route distribution had a higher-than-average long-tail request distribution; some workers experienced eviction while rebuilding cache causing synchronous fallback and queueing.
3) Corrective actions proposed (fast/med/long):
   - Fast (0–24h): Block background warmups on Dedicated pools that serve peak customer traffic; apply routing soft-pins; increase min-capacity by 15–25%.
   - Medium (3–7d): Introduce maintenance-window policy and smarter warmup orchestration tied to traffic forecasts; add KV allocation backpressure metrics and alerting.
   - Long (2–6w): Model cold-start mitigation: pre-cached kernel shards + per-customer cache reservation; autoscaler policy refinement to avoid simultaneous de-register/re-register of workers serving same routes.

Attachments: novaris_rca_draft.pdf (contains timeline, logs, and proposed owner list).

Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
